# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1504._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `_rebuildAllRequests` drops the running cumulative — every request's `cumulativeUsage` equals its own usage only (red CI: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)`)**

The loop passes `null` as the cumulative seed on **every** iteration and discards the return value of `_foldRequestNumber`:

```dart
for (var i = 0; i < facts.length; i++) {
  _reqPositions[facts[i]] = i;
  _foldRequestNumber(i, facts[i], null);   // ← running cumulative lost
}
```

This is the fallback derivation that `appendAll` always takes (single publish, `_reqSorted == null`), so **the bulk-replay / CLI path returns wrong cumulative usage**. Confirmed against the failing CI test `test/integration/trajectory/cli_integration_test.dart` (`cost prints the usage table with the cumulative line`) and reproduced locally with a 4-request fixture (100/100/200 input tokens):

- expected: `session cumulative: in 400` (cum tokens 120 / 240 / 240 / 480)
- actual: `session cumulative: in 200` (cum tokens 120 / 120 / null / 240)

The live-tail path masked this in the PR's own gates because later suffix rebuilds (`_rebuildRequestsSuffix`) thread the cumulative correctly and overwrote the bad cache entries — but any host that goes through `appendAll` (the `fa trajectory cost` CLI, session open / branch page-in) gets per-request-only cumulative values. The PR description claims this path is "byte-identical to the pre-#1497 code" — it is not.

Fix (verified locally: all 201 `test/trajectory/` tests pass and the failing integration test goes green):

```dart
_reqCumulative = <Usage?>[];
Usage? cumulative;
for (var i = 0; i < facts.length; i++) {
  _reqPositions[facts[i]] = i;
  cumulative = _foldRequestNumber(i, facts[i], cumulative);
}
```

Please also add a regression test with **two or more usage-carrying facts** through `appendAll` asserting `cumulativeUsage` grows across requests — the current bulk-replay test uses a single fact, which passes even with this bug (see the sibling comment on the test).

---

### Thread 2 — `test/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the bulk-replay regression test uses a single request fact — it cannot catch a broken cumulative fold**

This test asserts `bulk.requests.single.cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens == 15`, but with exactly one usage-carrying fact, "cumulative" and "own usage" are indistinguishable — the test passes even when the fold seeds every row from `null` (the bug that broke `PTY/CLI integration` on this PR: `_rebuildAllRequests` passed `null` as the cumulative on every iteration, and `appendAll` always routes through that fallback).

Extend it to at least two usage-carrying assistant facts (e.g. 15 then 20 tokens) and assert the second request's cumulative is the **sum** (35), plus the same expectations on the per-append `live` builder so both publish paths are pinned:

```dart
expect(bulk.requests[1].cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens, 35);
expect(liveSnapshot.requests[1].cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens, 35);
```

A multi-fact version of this test fails on the current head and passes with the one-line `_rebuildAllRequests` fix.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `snapshotRowCopies` doc says "over this builder's life" but resets silently zero it**

The doc on this getter promises a lifetime total, but `_ChunkStore.reset()` sets `copiedRows = 0`, and `_rebuildAllRequests()` calls `_reqNumberRows.reset()` — so a mid-session `builder.reset()` or a request-fact resort silently restarts the counter from zero. Any long-running host that resets or triggers a resort under-reports the metric (and the scaling envelope becomes a since-last-reset figure, which is hard to reason about).

Either don't zero `copiedRows` in `reset()` (keep a separate since-reset figure if needed), or adjust the doc to "since the last reset / full request rebuild". Minor, but the counter is the deterministic guard the tests lean on — its semantics should be unambiguous.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: order-tie after a touch keeps the cached order, but the pre-#1497 full sort could order tied facts differently**

The resort guard only triggers when the bumped order moves strictly past the successor (`sorted[position + 1].order < fact.order`). Two facts can end up with **equal** orders (e.g. two assistant requests finalized while `_rows.length` is the same), and `List.sort` is not stable — the old code's full sort could place the tied pair in a different relative order than the cached one, so a snapshot can deviate from the pre-#1497 derivation in tie cases despite the "byte-identical" claim.

If exact old-code parity matters for ties, use `<=` here (resort on tie) — the fallback is rare, so the cost is negligible. If insertion-order-wins is an acceptable, arguably more predictable semantic, a one-line comment documenting the deliberate choice would be enough.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T18:25:16Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

# pr-1504: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append

## Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1504._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `_rebuildAllRequests` drops the running cumulative — every request's `cumulativeUsage` equals its own usage only (red CI: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)`)**

The loop passes `null` as the cumulative seed on **every** iteration and discards the return value of `_foldRequestNumber`:

```dart
for (var i = 0; i < facts.length; i++) {
  _reqPositions[facts[i]] = i;
  _foldRequestNumber(i, facts[i], null);   // ← running cumulative lost
}
```

This is the fallback derivation that `appendAll` always takes (single publish, `_reqSorted == null`), so **the bulk-replay / CLI path returns wrong cumulative usage**. Confirmed against the failing CI test `test/integration/trajectory/cli_integration_test.dart` (`cost prints the usage table with the cumulative line`) and reproduced locally with a 4-request fixture (100/100/200 input tokens):

- expected: `session cumulative: in 400` (cum tokens 120 / 240 / 240 / 480)
- actual: `session cumulative: in 200` (cum tokens 120 / 120 / null / 240)

The live-tail path masked this in the PR's own gates because later suffix rebuilds (`_rebuildRequestsSuffix`) thread the cumulative correctly and overwrote the bad cache entries — but any host that goes through `appendAll` (the `fa trajectory cost` CLI, session open / branch page-in) gets per-request-only cumulative values. The PR description claims this path is "byte-identical to the pre-#1497 code" — it is not.

Fix (verified locally: all 201 `test/trajectory/` tests pass and the failing integration test goes green):

```dart
_reqCumulative = <Usage?>[];
Usage? cumulative;
for (var i = 0; i < facts.length; i++) {
  _reqPositions[facts[i]] = i;
  cumulative = _foldRequestNumber(i, facts[i], cumulative);
}
```

Please also add a regression test with **two or more usage-carrying facts** through `appendAll` asserting `cumulativeUsage` grows across requests — the current bulk-replay test uses a single fact, which passes even with this bug (see the sibling comment on the test).

---

### Thread 2 — `test/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the bulk-replay regression test uses a single request fact — it cannot catch a broken cumulative fold**

This test asserts `bulk.requests.single.cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens == 15`, but with exactly one usage-carrying fact, "cumulative" and "own usage" are indistinguishable — the test passes even when the fold seeds every row from `null` (the bug that broke `PTY/CLI integration` on this PR: `_rebuildAllRequests` passed `null` as the cumulative on every iteration, and `appendAll` always routes through that fallback).

Extend it to at least two usage-carrying assistant facts (e.g. 15 then 20 tokens) and assert the second request's cumulative is the **sum** (35), plus the same expectations on the per-append `live` builder so both publish paths are pinned:

```dart
expect(bulk.requests[1].cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens, 35);
expect(liveSnapshot.requests[1].cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens, 35);
```

A multi-fact version of this test fails on the current head and passes with the one-line `_rebuildAllRequests` fix.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `snapshotRowCopies` doc says "over this builder's life" but resets silently zero it**

The doc on this getter promises a lifetime total, but `_ChunkStore.reset()` sets `copiedRows = 0`, and `_rebuildAllRequests()` calls `_reqNumberRows.reset()` — so a mid-session `builder.reset()` or a request-fact resort silently restarts the counter from zero. Any long-running host that resets or triggers a resort under-reports the metric (and the scaling envelope becomes a since-last-reset figure, which is hard to reason about).

Either don't zero `copiedRows` in `reset()` (keep a separate since-reset figure if needed), or adjust the doc to "since the last reset / full request rebuild". Minor, but the counter is the deterministic guard the tests lean on — its semantics should be unambiguous.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: order-tie after a touch keeps the cached order, but the pre-#1497 full sort could order tied facts differently**

The resort guard only triggers when the bumped order moves strictly past the successor (`sorted[position + 1].order < fact.order`). Two facts can end up with **equal** orders (e.g. two assistant requests finalized while `_rows.length` is the same), and `List.sort` is not stable — the old code's full sort could place the tied pair in a different relative order than the cached one, so a snapshot can deviate from the pre-#1497 derivation in tie cases despite the "byte-identical" claim.

If exact old-code parity matters for ties, use `<=` here (resort on tie) — the fallback is rare, so the cost is negligible. If insertion-order-wins is an acceptable, arguably more predictable semantic, a one-line comment documenting the deliberate choice would be enough.

---

### Thread 5

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: One blocking correctness bug: `_rebuildAllRequests` seeds every fold with a `null` cumulative and discards the running value, so `appendAll` (the `fa trajectory cost` CLI / session-open path) reports per-request usage as the cumulative — failing CI (`PTY/CLI integration` shard 2/3, `cost prints the usage table`, expected `session cumulative: in 400`, got `in 200`). The chunked copy-on-write store, lazy `recordLocations`, tail-truncation discard, and suffix-fold design are otherwise sound; I verified snapshot immutability under later appends and could not break the COW/chunk-sharing invariants.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `_rebuildAllRequests` drops the running cumulative (one-line fix: thread the return value); verified locally — all 201 `test/trajectory/` tests plus the failing integration test pass with it.
- ⚠️ The new bulk-replay test uses a single request fact, which cannot detect the broken fold — extend to ≥2 usage-carrying facts asserting summed cumulative on both `appendAll` and per-append paths.

**Next Steps**:
1. Apply the one-line cumulative threading fix in `_rebuildAllRequests`.
2. Strengthen the bulk-replay test to cover multi-fact cumulative folding (live vs bulk).
3. Optional: clarify `snapshotRowCopies` lifetime semantics under `reset()`/resort, and document the order-tie behavior in `_requestFactTouched`.

---

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the bulk-replay regression test still uses a single request fact — it cannot catch the broken cumulative fold (re-review; unchanged at head `9d34bb98e`)**

This test still asserts `bulk.requests.single.cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens == 15`. With exactly one usage-carrying fact, "cumulative" and "own usage" are indistinguishable — the test passes even while `_rebuildAllRequests` seeds every row from `null` (the blocking bug on this PR, still present and still red in `PTY/CLI integration`). A regression guard that cannot fail while the guarded bug is live is not a guard.

Extend it to at least two usage-carrying assistant facts (e.g. 15 then 20 tokens) and assert the second request's cumulative is the **sum** (35), plus the same expectations on the per-append `live` builder so both publish paths are pinned:

```dart

expect(liveSnapshot.requests[1].cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens, 35);
```

A multi-fact version of this test fails on the current head and passes with the one-line `_rebuildAllRequests` fix.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `snapshotRowCopies` doc says "over this builder's life" but resets silently zero it (re-review; unchanged at head `9d34bb98e`)**

The doc on this getter (and on `_ChunkStore.copiedRows`) promises a lifetime total, but `_ChunkStore.reset()` sets `copiedRows = 0`, and `_rebuildAllRequests()` calls `_reqNumberRows.reset()` — so a mid-session `builder.reset()` or a request-fact resort silently restarts the counter from zero. Any long-running host that resets or triggers a resort under-reports the metric, and the scaling envelope becomes a since-last-reset figure.

Either don't zero `copiedRows` in `reset()` (keep a separate since-reset figure if needed), or adjust the doc to "since the last reset / full request rebuild". # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T18:25:16Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `_rebuildAllRequests` drops the running cumulative — every request's `cumulativeUsage` equals its own usage only (red CI: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)`)**

The loop passes `null` as the cumulative seed on **every** iteration and discards the return value of `_foldRequestNumber`:

```dart
for (var i = 0; i < facts.length; i++) {
  _reqPositions[facts[i]] = i;
  _foldRequestNumber(i, facts[i], null);   // ← running cumulative lost
}
```

This is the fallback derivation that `appendAll` always takes (single publish, `_reqSorted == null`), so **the bulk-replay / CLI path returns wrong cumulative usage**. Confirmed against the failing CI test `test/integration/trajectory/cli_integration_test.dart` (`cost prints the usage table with the cumulative line`) and reproduced locally with a 4-request fixture (100/100/200 input tokens):

- expected: `session cumulative: in 400` (cum tokens 120 / 240 / 240 / 480)
- actual: `session cumulative: in 200` (cum tokens 120 / 120 / null / 240)

The live-tail path masked this in the PR's own gates because later suffix rebuilds (`_rebuildRequestsSuffix`) thread the cumulative correctly and overwrote the bad cache entries — but any host that goes through `appendAll` (the `fa trajectory cost` CLI, session open / branch page-in) gets per-request-only cumulative values. The PR description claims this path is "byte-identical to the pre-#1497 code" — it is not.

Fix (verified locally: all 201 `test/trajectory/` tests pass and the failing integration test goes green):

```dart
_reqCumulative = <Usage?>[];
Usage? cumulative;
for (var i = 0; i < facts.length; i++) {
  _reqPositions[facts[i]] = i;
  cumulative = _foldRequestNumber(i, facts[i], cumulative);
}
```

Please also add a regression test with **two or more usage-carrying facts** through `appendAll` asserting `cumulativeUsage` grows across requests — the current bulk-replay test uses a single fact, which passes even with this bug (see the sibling comment on the test).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the bulk-replay regression test uses a single request fact — it cannot catch a broken cumulative fold**

This test asserts `bulk.requests.single.cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens == 15`, but with exactly one usage-carrying fact, "cumulative" and "own usage" are indistinguishable — the test passes even when the fold seeds every row from `null` (the bug that broke `PTY/CLI integration` on this PR: `_rebuildAllRequests` passed `null` as the cumulative on every iteration, and `appendAll` always routes through that fallback).

Extend it to at least two usage-carrying assistant facts (e.g. 15 then 20 tokens) and assert the second request's cumulative is the **sum** (35), plus the same expectations on the per-append `live` builder so both publish paths are pinned:

```dart
expect(bulk.requests[1].cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens, 35);
expect(liveSnapshot.requests[1].cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens, 35);
```

A multi-fact version of this test fails on the current head and passes with the one-line `_rebuildAllRequests` fix.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `snapshotRowCopies` doc says "over this builder's life" but resets silently zero it**

The doc on this getter promises a lifetime total, but `_ChunkStore.reset()` sets `copiedRows = 0`, and `_rebuildAllRequests()` calls `_reqNumberRows.reset()` — so a mid-session `builder.reset()` or a request-fact resort silently restarts the counter from zero. Any long-running host that resets or triggers a resort under-reports the metric (and the scaling envelope becomes a since-last-reset figure, which is hard to reason about).

Either don't zero `copiedRows` in `reset()` (keep a separate since-reset figure if needed), or adjust the doc to "since the last reset / full request rebuild". Minor, but the counter is the deterministic guard the tests lean on — its semantics should be unambiguous.

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. - 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T18:25:16Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).

# pr-1504: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append

## Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1504._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `_rebuildAllRequests` drops the running cumulative — every request's `cumulativeUsage` equals its own usage only (red CI: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)`)**

The loop passes `null` as the cumulative seed on **every** iteration and discards the return value of `_foldRequestNumber`:

```dart
for (var i = 0; i < facts.length; i++) {
  _reqPositions[facts[i]] = i;
  _foldRequestNumber(i, facts[i], null);   // ← running cumulative lost
}
```

This is the fallback derivation that `appendAll` always takes (single publish, `_reqSorted == null`), so **the bulk-replay / CLI path returns wrong cumulative usage**. Confirmed against the failing CI test `test/integration/trajectory/cli_integration_test.dart` (`cost prints the usage table with the cumulative line`) and reproduced locally with a 4-request fixture (100/100/200 input tokens):

- expected: `session cumulative: in 400` (cum tokens 120 / 240 / 240 / 480)
- actual: `session cumulative: in 200` (cum tokens 120 / 120 / null / 240)

The live-tail path masked this in the PR's own gates because later suffix rebuilds (`_rebuildRequestsSuffix`) thread the cumulative correctly and overwrote the bad cache entries — but any host that goes through `appendAll` (the `fa trajectory cost` CLI, session open / branch page-in) gets per-request-only cumulative values. The PR description claims this path is "byte-identical to the pre-#1497 code" — it is not.

Fix (verified locally: all 201 `test/trajectory/` tests pass and the failing integration test goes green):

```dart
_reqCumulative = <Usage?>[];
Usage? cumulative;
for (var i = 0; i < facts.length; i++) {
  _reqPositions[facts[i]] = i;
  cumulative = _foldRequestNumber(i, facts[i], cumulative);
}
```

Please also add a regression test with **two or more usage-carrying facts** through `appendAll` asserting `cumulativeUsage` grows across requests — the current bulk-replay test uses a single fact, which passes even with this bug (see the sibling comment on the test).

---

### Thread 2 — `test/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the bulk-replay regression test uses a single request fact — it cannot catch a broken cumulative fold**

This test asserts `bulk.requests.single.cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens == 15`, but with exactly one usage-carrying fact, "cumulative" and "own usage" are indistinguishable — the test passes even when the fold seeds every row from `null` (the bug that broke `PTY/CLI integration` on this PR: `_rebuildAllRequests` passed `null` as the cumulative on every iteration, and `appendAll` always routes through that fallback).

Extend it to at least two usage-carrying assistant facts (e.g. 15 then 20 tokens) and assert the second request's cumulative is the **sum** (35), plus the same expectations on the per-append `live` builder so both publish paths are pinned:

```dart
expect(bulk.requests[1].cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens, 35);
expect(liveSnapshot.requests[1].cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens, 35);
```

A multi-fact version of this test fails on the current head and passes with the one-line `_rebuildAllRequests` fix.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `snapshotRowCopies` doc says "over this builder's life" but resets silently zero it**

The doc on this getter promises a lifetime total, but `_ChunkStore.reset()` sets `copiedRows = 0`, and `_rebuildAllRequests()` calls `_reqNumberRows.reset()` — so a mid-session `builder.reset()` or a request-fact resort silently restarts the counter from zero. Any long-running host that resets or triggers a resort under-reports the metric (and the scaling envelope becomes a since-last-reset figure, which is hard to reason about).

Either don't zero `copiedRows` in `reset()` (keep a separate since-reset figure if needed), or adjust the doc to "since the last reset / full request rebuild". Minor, but the counter is the deterministic guard the tests lean on — its semantics should be unambiguous.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: order-tie after a touch keeps the cached order, but the pre-#1497 full sort could order tied facts differently**

The resort guard only triggers when the bumped order moves strictly past the successor (`sorted[position + 1].order < fact.order`). Two facts can end up with **equal** orders (e.g. two assistant requests finalized while `_rows.length` is the same), and `List.sort` is not stable — the old code's full sort could place the tied pair in a different relative order than the cached one, so a snapshot can deviate from the pre-#1497 derivation in tie cases despite the "byte-identical" claim.

If exact old-code parity matters for ties, use `<=` here (resort on tie) — the fallback is rare, so the cost is negligible. If insertion-order-wins is an acceptable, arguably more predictable semantic, a one-line comment documenting the deliberate choice would be enough.

---

### Thread 5

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1504
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1504
- **Title**: perf(1497): incremental TrajectorySnapshotBuilder publishing — O(delta) per append
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1497-trajectory-append-o-n` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +595
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T17:08:27Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T18:25:16Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1497

## Hot path (confirmed)

Every `append()`/`applyEvent()` materialized a snapshot by copying every ledger row (`List.of`), rebuilding the whole `recordLocations` map, and re-sorting + re-folding cumulative usage over **every** request fact — O(n) per append, O(n²) per live session. Bulk `appendAll` was already linear; the live tail was the slide-show.

**Before/after (4 records/turn synthetic, warmed VM, standalone Dart SDK 3.13.5):**

| shape | before (main @ 0c602bf47e) | after |
|---|---|---|
| live tail, 65k `append()` = 65k snapshots | **380 895 ms (~6.3 min)** | **92 ms (~4 100×)** |
| per-append cost, 1k → 80k records | 60 µs → ~5-10 ms (grows linearly with n) | flat **~1.5-2.3 µs** |
| bulk `appendAll` 65k | ~100 ms (already linear) | ~98 ms (unchanged) |

## Fix (algorithmic, per the card)

- **Chunked row store with copy-on-write publishing**: 512-row chunks; a snapshot publishes an immutable chunk-pointer list (O(chunks) refs); the next cycle clones a chunk before its first in-place write. Published snapshots stay byte-identical and immutable.
- **Lazy `recordLocations`**: derived on first access per snapshot (no lib/ reader touches it on the append path; identical content to the eager map).
- **Incremental requests cache**: cached sorted-fact order + built numbers + running cumulative usage; a snapshot rebuilds only the suffix at/after the first touched fact. New facts always fold in at the sorted tail (order = row count at creation, which only grows); anything the incremental path cannot prove order-stable falls back to the **exact full sort** the old code ran.
- **Streamed-row replacement** truncates a contiguous tail and drops only the cut tool-row indexes; non-tail placement keeps the legacy filter + full rebuild.

## Regression guards (bounded, not flake-prone)

- `snapshotRowCopies` counter (the `chainWalkHops` pattern, deterministic): measured **150 rows/append**, envelope 600/append — the quadratic shape copies ~n/2 rows per append and fails it by 3 orders of magnitude. No wall-clock ratio asserted: the #358 flake lesson, plus a measured 60× JIT-tier cliff on cold first runs.
- Absolute 8 s budget on a 20k live-tail run (fixed: <100 ms warm, ~2.1 s worst cold; pre-fix measured 31 s) — well under the 30 s per-test timeout cap.
- 50k `appendAll` open-budget check (issue acceptance), snapshot-immutability-under-later-appends (chunk sharing + lazy locations freeze), bulk-replay request folding (facts created + finalized between snapshots).

## Gates

- `dart analyze`: 0 issues on changed files (repo-wide 132 pre-existing infos, identical with the change stashed).
- `dart test test/trajectory/` 200 ✓ + event-handler/compaction 31 ✓ + `test/integration/trajectory/snapshot_builder_integration_test.dart` 6 ✓ (live-vs-replay requests compared field-by-field).
- `dart format` clean.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: all three card items — profile bench (1k/10k/50k/65k synthetic, growth asserted), per-append copying eliminated (structural sharing + invalidatable derived cache; `_snapshot` now O(delta)), snapshots cheap (shared refs + suffix fold; 546 ms instrumented mean → µs).
Remaining (not in scope here): the fold path itself shows a cold-run JIT-tier cliff (~100 µs/append unwarmed, ~1.7 µs warmed — same code pre/post, deterministic counters unaffected); a follow-up could warm or restructure `_appendRecord` if cold-start latency ever matters.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `_rebuildAllRequests` drops the running cumulative — every request's `cumulativeUsage` equals its own usage only (red CI: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)`)**

The loop passes `null` as the cumulative seed on **every** iteration and discards the return value of `_foldRequestNumber`:

```dart
for (var i = 0; i < facts.length; i++) {
  _reqPositions[facts[i]] = i;
  _foldRequestNumber(i, facts[i], null);   // ← running cumulative lost
}
```

This is the fallback derivation that `appendAll` always takes (single publish, `_reqSorted == null`), so **the bulk-replay / CLI path returns wrong cumulative usage**. Confirmed against the failing CI test `test/integration/trajectory/cli_integration_test.dart` (`cost prints the usage table with the cumulative line`) and reproduced locally with a 4-request fixture (100/100/200 input tokens):

- expected: `session cumulative: in 400` (cum tokens 120 / 240 / 240 / 480)
- actual: `session cumulative: in 200` (cum tokens 120 / 120 / null / 240)

The live-tail path masked this in the PR's own gates because later suffix rebuilds (`_rebuildRequestsSuffix`) thread the cumulative correctly and overwrote the bad cache entries — but any host that goes through `appendAll` (the `fa trajectory cost` CLI, session open / branch page-in) gets per-request-only cumulative values. The PR description claims this path is "byte-identical to the pre-#1497 code" — it is not.

Fix (verified locally: all 201 `test/trajectory/` tests pass and the failing integration test goes green):

```dart
_reqCumulative = <Usage?>[];
Usage? cumulative;
for (var i = 0; i < facts.length; i++) {
  _reqPositions[facts[i]] = i;
  cumulative = _foldRequestNumber(i, facts[i], cumulative);
}
```

Please also add a regression test with **two or more usage-carrying facts** through `appendAll` asserting `cumulativeUsage` grows across requests — the current bulk-replay test uses a single fact, which passes even with this bug (see the sibling comment on the test).

expect(bulk.requests[1].cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens, 35);
expect(liveSnapshot.requests[1].cumulativeUsage?.totalTokens, 35);

A multi-fact version of this test fails on the current head and passes with the one-line `_rebuildAllRequests` fix.

The doc on this getter (and on `_ChunkStore.copiedRows`) promises a lifetime total, but `_ChunkStore.reset()` sets `copiedRows = 0`, and `_rebuildAllRequests()` calls `_reqNumberRows.reset()` — so a mid-session `builder.reset()` or a request-fact resort silently restarts the counter from zero. Any long-running host that resets or triggers a resort under-reports the metric, and the scaling envelope becomes a since-last-reset figure.

Either don't zero `copiedRows` in `reset()` (keep a separate since-reset figure if needed), or adjust the doc to "since the last reset / full request rebuild". Minor, but the counter is the deterministic guard the tests lean on — its semantics should be unambiguous. (Related: `_ChunkStore.truncate(0)` also replaces `_chunks[0]` without counting the dropped rows, same undercount class.)

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: order-tie after a touch keeps the cached order, but the pre-#1497 full sort could order tied facts differently (re-review; unchanged at head `9d34bb98e`)**

The resort guard still only triggers when the bumped order moves strictly past the successor (`sorted[position + 1].order < fact.order`). Two facts can end up with **equal** orders (e.g. two assistant requests finalized while `_rows.length` is the same), and `List.sort` is not stable — the old code's full sort could place the tied pair in a different relative order than the cached one, so a snapshot can deviate from the pre-#1497 derivation in tie cases despite the "byte-identical" claim.

If exact old-code parity matters for ties, use `<=` here (resort on tie) — the fallback is rare, so the cost is negligible. If insertion-order-wins is an acceptable, arguably more predictable semantic, a one-line comment documenting the deliberate choice would be enough.
